$comment: Per-field provenance. Only method='human' counts toward governance.verification.status='verified'.

delivery_paradigm.note: structural categorisation (this profile covers file-based audio-only deliveries); EBU R128 is a loudness measurement standard and doesn't discuss delivery mode. Same treatment as id/name.

assets.audio.loudness.standards[0].name.matched: EBU R 128-2023  Audio loudness normalisation & permitted maximum level

assets.audio.loudness.standards[0].targe.matched: the Programme Loudness Level shall be normalised to a Target Level of −23.0 LUFS

assets.audio.loudness.standards[0].toler.matched: ±1.0 LU is permitted [when Target Level is not achievable practically, e.g. live]; ±0.2 LU is allowed for QC/measurement-workflow tolerance
assets.audio.loudness.standards[0].toler.note: profile asserts 0.5, but current R128-2023 states neither 1.0 (the live/impractical exception) nor 0.2 (QC measurement tolerance) as a general tolerance. 0.5 matches the document's OWN changelog note that a 2014-vintage (V3) edition once used ±0.5 LU — possibly a stale figure carried over from an older R128 edition. FLAGGED for human ruling: not corrected here, confidence too low to pick a replacement value.

assets.audio.loudness.standards[0].juris.note: EBU R128 is nominally a European standard but is a de facto global reference used well outside EBU membership; 'global' is a categorical description of this profile's intended applicability, not a value the standard document itself states.

assets.audio.loudness.true_peak_max.matched: the True Peak Level of a programme shall not exceed −1 dBTP

id.note: authoring identifier, not a value asserted by the cited source document. Same treatment as clearcast_commercials.

name.note: authored title, not a value the source document states. Same treatment as clearcast_commercials.
